Source.evidence_source: ['/page/4/Text/6', 'The Children\'s Depression Inventory (Kovacs, 1981) is the most commonly used self-report measure of  depression for children 7 to 17 years of age.'] ['/page/4/Text/7', 'The Child Depression Scale (CDS; Reynolds, in press), a self-report  measure for children 8 to 13, was also employed to assess the severity of  depression.'] ['/page/4/Text/8', 'The Children\'s Depression Rating Scale-Revised (CDRS-R; Poznanski et al., 1984) is a semistructured interview  schedule appropriate for children ages 6 to 12.'] ['/page/4/Text/9', 'Each child\'s mother completed a portion of the  Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL; Achenbach & Edlebrock, 1979). The internalizing, depression, and social withdrawal subscales were employed.']
